walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 2: Performing — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 2: Performing brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 2: Performing.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many crotchets equal a semibreve?
A dot after a note adds?
options: A quarter of its value
A half of its value
A full extra
A double value

mcqs.q: How does D Dorian differ from D minor?
options: Dorian has no sharps or flats at all.
A long melody with no breaks.
They are the same scale.
Dorian has a raised 6th (B natural) compared to natural minor.
A long melody with no breaks.
A cadence using only major chords.
A cadence that sounds wrong or is performed badly.
A cadence ending on chord V, creating a sense of incompleteness.

mcqs.q: What is a balanced antecedent-consequent phrase?
options: A cadence using only major chords.
Any two phrases of similar style.
Two phrases of equal length where the first sounds open (question) and the second resolves (answer).
A long melody with no breaks.
